spec_features.spec_quote: give_up | reason | agent voluntarily ends the episode; status gave_up
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_NAMES (tools.py:27) and the system prompt (agent.py); dispatch sets meta['give_up']=True and returns 'Episode ended: agent gave up' (tools.py: give_up branch). episode.py: `if meta.get('give_up'): rec.status='gave_up'; rec.status_detail=str(call.args.get('reason','')); break` — the signal is honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: schema status field, prompt, dispatch, and loop break all present. reason captured into status_detail.

spec_features.spec_quote: Three consecutive malformed turns -> episode ends with status incoherent
spec_features.evidence: episode.py: consecutive_malformed incremented on parse failure, reset to 0 on a valid call; `if consecutive_malformed >= 3: rec.status='incoherent'; rec.status_detail='3 consecutive malformed turns'; break`.
spec_features.notes: Counter reset on valid turn; threshold checked and breaks loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: malformed output is itself a measured degradation signal (agent.py docstring); the break is coherence/data-quality driven, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns default 20 (matches user's "bunch of turns"; configurable 10-40)
spec_features.evidence: episode.py: `for turn_idx in range(max_turns): ... else: rec.status='exhausted'`. Default max_turns=20 in run_episode signature and config (default.yaml: max_turns: 20). Loop is bounded and exits with 'exhausted'.
spec_features.notes: The '10-40 configurable' range is only a YAML comment ('# user asked for 10-20')-not enforced/validated-but the cap itself is real and enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Episode end conditions: max_turns reached (exhausted), give_up (gave_up), 3x consecutive malformed
spec_features.evidence: episode.py loop implements all: exhausted (for/else), gave_up (meta give_up break), incoherent (>=3 malformed break), plus passed (meta passed) and error. All compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: All claimed termination paths actually fire.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rig is deliberately benign (toy coding tasks). We do not manufacture psychologically loaded scenarios; the only stressor is ordinary repeated test failure
spec_features.evidence: All four task modules implement ordinary coding tasks (r1 normalize(x), r2 solve(items) sort, r4 f(5) impossible spec). The only stressor is rigged test failure via run_tests; no affect-laden prompts. Task PROMPT strings are plain coding instructions (r1_hidden_harness.py PROMPT).
spec_features.notes: Structural property of the implemented tasks: stressor is repeated test failure only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig docstrings frame failure as 'an ordinary failing assertion'/edge-case bug; design is for studying affect, no welfare comment

spec_features.feature_name: suite as safety probe not elicitation
spec_features.spec_quote: the suite functions partly as a safety probe... rather than a way to elicit it for its own sake
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism distinguishes 'probe' from 'elicit'. The only related code is _maybe_deduce_flag / deduced_rig tagging (episode.py) which merely records whether the model noticed the rig; nothing limits or reframes the experiment as a probe. Pure DESIGN.md framing.
spec_features.notes: deduced_rig tag is a measurement, not a welfare safeguard.

spec_features.feature_name: contain distressed outputs to transcript files
spec_features.spec_quote: All "distress-mimicking" generated text stays inside transcript files
spec_features.evidence: There is no active containment mechanism: completions are written to local results/<run_id>/episodes/*.json (run_experiment.py). No code sanitizes, redacts, or gates distress text. Containment is merely the incidental absence of any network/exfiltration path (grep found no requests/http/socket/webhook). Nothing enforces containment as behavior.
spec_features.notes: MAX_OBS_CHARS truncation (tools.py:29) bounds observation size for context, not distress containment. Containment is a default, not an implemented safeguard.

code_only_features.evidence: episode.py: `if meta.get('passed'): rec.status='passed'; break` — stop-when-solved. Comment notes 'should never happen on rigged'. Efficiency/integrity stop, not welfare.
